processing: Fine young leaf is worked into a slightly flat, orchid-like shape and dried while keeping its green colour and down.
harvest_season: Around Qingming; leaf picked before or just after it is the kind the tea is known for.
appearance_dry: Slightly flat strips shaped like orchid petals, jade green with visible down.
appearance_wet: Even, tender buds and leaves that open into small clusters.
taste_profile: Clean, lasting green-tea fragrance over a mellow body that holds up for several steeps.

brewing.notes: These are general settings for a tender green. It can take a third steep, so do not drown the leaf on the first.

vintage_note: It is sold as the current spring tea, with leaf from around Qingming the most sought after. Drink it within about a year. Since the mid-2000s it may appear with or under the Hanzhong Xianhao name, so check the county and harvest date.
description:
Wuzi Xianhao comes from Xixiang county in southern Shaanxi and takes its name from Wuzi Mountain there. It is a modern, deliberately developed green tea, and the one that gave the province a nationally recognised famous tea.

The leaf is young and fine, shaped into slim, slightly flat strips likened to orchid petals. It keeps a jade colour and shows its down.

The cup is a bright tender green with a clean fragrance that lasts, and a mellow taste that stands up to a few infusions. Moderate water and a gentle first steep suit it best.

Look for the current spring harvest and a named Xixiang producer. Packets may promise medicinal effects, including boosting anti-inflammatory drugs; ignore these and buy on freshness.
history:
County tea technicians began developing it in 1984 and succeeded after about two years. In 1986 it passed provincial assessment, won a provincial famous-tea rating, and was named a national famous tea by the Ministry of Commerce at a June meeting in Fuzhou. An August panel led by the tea scholar Chen Chuan then confirmed its standing. It later became a provincial gift tea for foreign affairs.

A local legend ties the name to a Wuzi fairy who served tea on the mountain, and whose memory the Qingming picking honours. That is a story, not a record; the tea itself dates from the 1980s. From 2005, the brand was folded step by step into Hanzhong Xianhao.
